t: You're at Hyde Park Gardens, two roads running beside the north-western corner of Hyde Park. The grand white stucco houses date from the early nineteenth century and are now mostly divided into flats. Numbers one to twenty-three share a large private garden, and the High Commission of Sri Lanka is here. The cleric Charles Chichester died here in 1858. He was English, and that's the extent of what's recorded, but it fits a terrace that has long been a distinguished address.
